title: OneDrive and SharePoint: annotate sensitivity-label protected PDFs in the web viewer
summary: Hold: the label-permissions command omits the encryption parameters that its reference says make the rights parameter meaningful. The roadmap facts and narrowly stated documentation gaps are supported; the label-permissions UI route also stops early and needs a minor correction.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: PDF sensitivity-label support can be enabled in Microsoft Purview portal at Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Policies > Auto-labeling policies ... if you see a message Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling, select this banner to confirm you want to turn on PDF protection for files in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF $true enables existing PDF sensitivity-label support.
claims.quote: -EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF ... Allows tenant admins to turn on support for PDFs with sensitivity labels ... True - Enables support for PDFs.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Running Set-SPOTenant requires the SharePoint Online administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Online administrator to run the cmdlet.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls
claims.claim: Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels in the Microsoft Purview portal is the route given for managing label encryption permissions.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels ... To edit an existing label, select it, and then select the Edit label icon.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and the matching rendered path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > label > Edit label > Define the scope for this label > Files & other data assets > Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected > Control access > Access control > Configure access control settings > Assign permissions now > Assign permissions > Choose permissions'. Set controls[1].ui.docs and its rendered Learn link to https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels, which documents the permission settings; retain create-sensitivity-labels in sources for the editing route.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <MasterIdParameter> -EncryptionRightsDefinitions <EncryptionRightsDefinitionsParameter> is the call that changes users' encryption usage rights.
claims.quote: This parameter is meaningful only when the EncryptionEnabled parameter value is either $true or $false and the EncryptionProtectionType parameter value is Template.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].api.call and the matching rendered call with 'Set-Label -Identity <MasterIdParameter> -EncryptionEnabled $true -EncryptionProtectionType Template -EncryptionRightsDefinitions <EncryptionRightsDefinitionsParameter>'. The reference explicitly conditions EncryptionRightsDefinitions on these encryption parameters; the replacement keeps encryption enabled while setting template-based rights.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The label's Access control page offers Assign permissions now for administrator-assigned encryption permissions.
claims.quote: On the Access control page ... Configure access control settings: Turns on encryption with rights management ... Assign permissions now, so that you determine exactly which users get which permissions to content with that label.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: For Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo, enabling PDF support requires connecting to each geo-location and running the command separately.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo: Similarly to the instructions to run the PowerShell command to enable support for sensitivity labels, you must connect to each of your geo-locations, and then run the command to enable support for PDFs.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: For labels using Assign permissions now, changed encryption settings for users or permissions apply to existing encrypted items when users authenticate with the encryption service.
claims.quote: For items that are already labeled with encryption and the assign permissions now option, when you change the encryption settings for users or permissions, the new settings will be applied for existing items when users authenticate with the encryption service.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Users with an existing use licence receive changed permissions after the licence expires and they reauthenticate, rather than immediately.
claims.quote: However, if users have already opened an encrypted document or email, they won't get the new settings until their use license has expired and they must reauthenticate.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The roadmap describes user annotation in the browser, not an automated or agent action.
claims.quote: With this update, users who have the appropriate usage rights can annotate these protected PDFs in place in their browser while preserving the file's sensitivity label, encryption, and usage rights when changes are saved.
